A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REVISOR framework. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references; v3 adds readable supplementary material in Sections 7–11.

before.justification: v1 reports original REVISOR evaluations on video understanding and temporal grounding benchmarks, reward and training-data ablations, and reasoning and retrieval analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and reports additional grounding metrics, reward-weight configurations, and qualitative case studies.

M1.justification: The Qwen2.5-VL-7B backbone, two-stage segment selection and visual reflection procedure, and DADR reward remain unchanged. The additional sampling, prompt, and KL-regularization details document implementation without establishing a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: The training datasets, four long-video understanding benchmarks, motivational evaluation datasets, and Charades-STA/NExT-GQA grounding coverage are retained. The supplementary data breakdown and illustrative cases do not establish additional tasks, datasets, or distinct test scenarios.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in the retained experiments are unchanged. v3 Table 5 uses the same grounding baselines as Table 2, including VTimeLLM, iMOVE, TimeChat, VideoChat-TPO, and TVG-R1. Section 9 documents the text-reflection baseline already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: Table 5 expands reported grounding evaluation from R@0.7 and mIoU to include R@0.3 and R@0.5. Table 6 adds three reward-weight configurations. Existing benchmark settings are retained; newly disclosed sampling rates and training-step counts do not establish revisions to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Table 6 extends the existing reward sensitivity analysis with weight pairs (0.45, 0.45), (0.5, 0.4), and (0.8, 0.1). Figures 7–9 add successful detail, scene-understanding, and counting cases; Figure 10 illustrates reasoning and segment selection across training checkpoints. These supplement questions already investigated in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent evaluation-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The unchanged eight-rollout training setting does not constitute repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The original benchmark and ablation scores are retained. v3 adds grounding recall results, including REVISOR's 76.5 R@0.3 on Charades-STA and 25.5 R@0.5 on NExT-GQA, three additional ablation rows, and qualitative case outcomes. These expand supporting results without changing the headline findings.

T1.justification: The inference, optimization, and reward definitions in Equations 1–7 are unchanged. v3 introduces no new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: diagnosing text-only reflection limitations, proposing tool-assisted visual reflection, and using DADR to learn useful review segments without additional supervised fine-tuning or external models.

C2.justification: Section 8.3 adds interpretations of excessively answer-heavy and nearly balanced reward weights, explaining proposed tradeoffs between localization and reasoning. Section 10 connects illustrative cases to detail capture, scene understanding, counting, and training-time refinement. The earlier mechanism explanations remain largely intact.

D1.justification: The supplement substantially expands reproducibility information: 1 FPS initial sampling, 2 FPS review sampling, timestamp overlays, 792 optimization steps, omitted KL regularization, per-source sample counts and selection procedures, baseline training details, and complete reasoning/system/tool prompts in Figures 11–13. These are newly documented details, not demonstrated changes to the underlying implementation.

R1.justification: The same 62 references are retained, but related work is substantively reframed. v3 emphasizes reasoning-conditioned segment selection and explicitly characterizes existing reflection as text-centric, while reducing v1's detailed discussion of Look-Back and Reflection-V to generic citations.

P1.justification: Most main-text wording is preserved. Related work is rewritten and moved from main Section 6 to supplementary Section 7; new supplementary sections and cross-references organize the added material. The experimental overview, an author affiliation, and the corresponding-author designation also change.

P2.justification: v3 adds substantial supplementary visual presentation: a dataset-composition chart, four illustrated case/training figures, and three prompt-template panels in Figures 6–13. Tables 5–6 provide expanded displays of the grounding comparison and reward ablation. The original figures and tables remain, with a corrected REVISOR legend spelling in Figure 5.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's brief setup, v3 makes implementation and baseline reproduction easier through explicit prompts, sampling rules, training duration, and data construction details. Additional metrics and ablations modestly strengthen the existing evidence. These benefits outweigh limited drawbacks: less nuanced discussion of prior visual-reflection work and a new arithmetic inconsistency in Section 8.3, where the claimed 4.3-point NExT-GQA margin is 4.7 points from Table 5's 25.5 versus 20.8. The method and headline empirical conclusions remain unchanged.
